summary: Steel tower moved to Ogidaki Mountain in 1968 and raised to 100 ft; a 2016 removal claim is unconfirmed, and sources disagree on current status.

facts.design: Steel tower, 80 ft, later raised to 100 ft
facts.status_note: Sources disagree: a 2005 statement describes radio relay use, a 2008 visitor found it standing, and a later edit claims removal in May 2016.

access.note: Reached over logging roads on Crown land. No source describes a gate or permit. The still-standing list asks visitors not to climb.

visit.trail_note: The 2008 route ran along a trail past an old towerman's shack, with the summit 1.1 km beyond it.

events.note: The 80-foot steel tower was moved to the summit of Ogidaki Mountain and increased to 100 feet, per the 2005 statement.
Radio relay communications use by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Quattra Communications, per the 2005 statement.
A hiker who summited on 22 July 2008 found the tower standing on the summit.
Claimed in a later edit to a 2008 visitor page. No ministry record in these sources confirms it.

evidence.supports: Original site north of the reserve, near Mekatlna Lake in Desbiens Township
evidence.quote: Originally, the Ogidaki Mountain fire tower was located north of the conservation reserve, near Mekatlna Lake in Desbiens Township.

evidence.supports: Relocated to the summit in 1968 and raised to 100 feet from 80 feet
evidence.quote: The 80-foot steel tower was relocated to the top of the Ogidaki Mountain in 1968, and increased to 100 feet.

evidence.supports: Last fire tower built in the province, according to MNR data
evidence.quote: According to MNR data, it was the last fire tower built in the province.

evidence.supports: Cabin built at the base of the mountain to accommodate staff
evidence.quote: Additionally, a cabin was constructed at the base of the mountain to accommodate staff.

evidence.supports: Cabin and part of the ladder dismantled in the late 1970s
evidence.quote: The cabin and a portion of ladder were dismantled in the late 1970s.

evidence.supports: Tower still used for radio relay by MNR and Quattra Communications
evidence.quote: The Ogidaki Tower remains utilized for radio relay communications by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Quattra Communications

evidence.supports: Tower described as a possible destination for curious sightseers
evidence.quote: Ogidaki Mountain and the fire tower located just outside of the northeastern portion of the conservation reserve may also be a choice destination for curious site-seers.

evidence.supports: Hill in the Algoma Highlands north of Sault Ste. Marie
evidence.quote: a high hill in the Algoma Highlands north of Sault Ste. Marie

evidence.supports: Summit reached by active and overgrown logging roads
evidence.quote: Today, although a series of active and overgrown logging roads lead to the summit, it is seldom visited.

evidence.supports: 2008 visitor found a standing tower and ministry shack; bottom ladder missing
evidence.quote: A well preserved fire tower and a Ministry of Natural Resources shack stood at the edge of the clearing; it’s bottom ladder missing, as to prevent people from climbing to the lookout.

evidence.supports: Later edit claims the ministry removed the tower in May 2016
evidence.quote: Ontario’s Ministry of Natural Resources removed the fire tower in May of 2016.

evidence.supports: Still-standing list entry for Mount Ogidaki Tower
List says the MNR no longer maintains the towers and asks visitors not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

evidence.supports: MNR decided as of 2013 to remove many still-standing towers
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these still standing towers.

sources.title: La Verendrye/Ogidaki Conservation Reserve Management Statement

notes_for_editor: The 2005 statement spells the old site Mekatlna Lake; the still-standing list spells the place Mekatina. Not resolved. Its claim that the tower was the last one built in the province is attributed to MNR data and not checked. The cabin and ladder removal is dated only to the late 1970s, so it has no event year. The 2016 removal rests on one edit note on ontariohighpoints.com; no ministry record was found, and the repo's expansion note cites the same edit. The brief's coordinates match the summit given by ontariohighpoints.com (N46.9922 W83.9839). Staffing today: no source found. The 2008 shack and the 2005 cabin may or may not be the same building.
